title: Between two sal trees
hookLine: at Kusinara he lies down on his right side; the trees blossom out of season (DN 16)
carry: rest is part of the path

lines: I'M TIRED. I WANT TO LIE DOWN.
cards: Visit a Buddhist temple and you may find him lying down. A huge golden figure, stretched out on his right side, head resting on one hand, eyes half closed, calm as a Sunday afternoon. It's easy to take it for a nap.
It's something else. It's today. After Cunda's meal, sick and weak, the Buddha walks on toward a small town called Kusinara.
He stops to rest along the way. He crosses a river. And at a grove of sal trees outside the town, he says to Ananda: I'm tired.

teach.h: HEAD TO THE NORTH, ON HIS RIGHT SIDE.
teach.b: Please, Ananda, he says, prepare a couch for me between these two sal trees, with my head to the north. Ananda does.
The Buddha lies down on his right side in what's called the lion's posture, one foot resting on the other, mindful and clearly aware. That's the pose in the great statues. Not sleep.
Awake, at rest, at the end.

teach.h: SAL TREES BLOOM OUT OF SEASON.
teach.b: Then, the text says, the twin sal trees burst into flower out of season, and blossoms drift down onto his body.
Flowers and sandalwood powder fall from the sky, and music plays from somewhere above, all in his honor. Here's the turn.

The Buddha tells Ananda, in effect: this is not how the one who found the way is truly honored. Not with flowers. Whoever lives by the teaching, practicing it well in small matters and great, honors him.
Even with the trees in bloom, he points away from the show and back to the practice. And the simplest part is quietly radical. He lay down.
The great teacher, who had walked from town to town all his teaching life, said he was tired, and rested.

teach.h: REST IS PART OF THE PATH.
teach.b: The path wasn't only effort; rest was part of it, especially here. In the same hours, the text tells of Ananda going off alone, leaning on a doorpost, and weeping.
My teacher is passing away, he says, the one who was so kind to me. The Buddha sends for him, comforts him, and praises him in front of everyone. Tomorrow, one more visitor arrives at the grove.

how: Reclining Buddha images, showing him on his right side between the sal trees at Kusinara, are found in temples across Asia, and pilgrims visit Kushinagar in India, where a large reclining image marks the place.

o: a river where pilgrims bathe at sunrise
a mountain cave where monks spent the rains
the small town where the Buddha lay down at the end

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.
p: on his right side, one foot on the other
the small town where he lay down

s: the reclining Buddha statues show him taking a nap
they show him lying down at Kusinara, awake, at the end of his life.
the Buddha said flowers are not how he is truly honored
Ananda wept, and the Buddha comforted and praised him
he sent for him and praised him before everyone.

games.q: you're dying, and the trees above you burst into flower in your honor. what do you tell your attendant?
o: that this is a sign of your greatness.
that true honor is living by the teaching.
to gather the flowers for a shrine.
games.why: he says this isn't how he's truly honored. whoever practices the teaching well, in small matters and great, honors him.

practice: If you can, lie down now, on your right side if that's comfortable, or on your back; if you can't, lean back and let your body be heavy. Feel what holds you up, and feel your breath slow down by itself.
There's nothing to do and nowhere to get to: rest, awake, and let this be practice too.

wordCard.voice: Kusinara. The small town near which the Buddha, tired after Cunda's meal, asked Ananda to prepare a couch between two sal trees and lay down to rest.

orig.note: Pali: the sal tree (Shorea robusta), under which, tradition says, the Buddha was also born.

carryVoice: Your line: rest is part of the path. Even the Buddha said: I'm tired. See you tomorrow.
